title: Jamshedpur Iron & Steel: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Jamshedpur steel borrower is either a primary plant (Tata Steel's ecosystem) or a secondary re-roller turning sponge iron, scrap and billets into TMT bars and structurals.** Cash comes from converting input tonnes into saleable tonnes fast; value sits in the spread between scrap/billet cost and TMT price, not in the asset. **So when a proposal lands, check the input mix first; if scrap share is high, ask for the landed scrap cost and supplier GST invoices.**

## Where cash and value sit
**Working capital is the whole game: inventory of billets and finished bars, plus receivables from dealers and government buyers.** Capex is heavy and lumpy (rolling mills, furnaces), so a re-roller's balance sheet is thin equity over large fixed assets. **Take monthly stock statements and a rolling 90-day sales register; if finished-goods days rise while sales fall, ask why before renewing.**

## What has changed now
**The local signal is mixed and the data call is Caution.** Jharkhand GST collections fell -0.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, a 6.3 pp gap [D] — a real local stress signal. Offsetting that, Jharkhand electricity demand rose +15.2% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% [D], and India-wide NIC 24 output grew +2.4% YoY with +3.4% Apr-to-date [D]. **Peer results are strong but margin-squeezed: JSW Steel's Q2 FY27 net profit was Rs.5,279 crore versus Rs.1,623 crore a year earlier [4], while Kirloskar Ferrous saw revenue up 17% y-o-y to INR 2,046.7 crore but EBITDA margin fall on coking coal and rupee depreciation [6].** Local news is thin on credit-relevant facts: a Tata Tiscon TMT seizure on the Hazaribagh-Barhi road [1], a shift-timing change for 2,800 Tata Steel employees [2], and Ghatkudi mine restarting after 15 months under an MDO model [3]. **Treat [1] as a brand-piracy and stolen-stock warning, not a demand signal.** Rating reports [8][9][10][11] are undated and generic; do not lean on them for this city.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue authorised TMT dealers and converters with documented offtake from a primary mill, and re-rollers with captive power and steady billet supply.** Avoid traders dealing in unbranded or grey TMT — the seizure [1] shows enforcement is active — and units whose GST turnover is flat or falling against the state's -0.2% [D]. **If a borrower cannot show primary-mill authorisation, decline.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending against stock and receivables, not land.** Take monthly stock and receivables statements, quarterly GST returns, and a personal guarantee. **Covenant a minimum monthly stock-turn and a maximum receivable days; if breached twice, freeze limits.** Collect from customer the exact turnover, stock days and receivable days — the pack gives none.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch electricity consumption versus reported production, GST filing gaps, and sudden dealer concentration.** If a unit's power draw falls while sales invoices hold, ask for dispatch records. If branded stock appears without authorisation, escalate.
